title: The Market Where Goods Remember Their Makers

features.name: memory-stall
features.desc-on-touch: Dried fruit arranged in careful lines, but each holds a photograph embedded in its flesh. The maker's face, slightly faded. Price tag reads: 'Remember who grew this.'

features.name: name-as-currency
features.desc-on-touch: Coins arranged in a spiral. Each one bears not a monarch's face but a surname. The vendor weighs them on a scale that reads only names. Trade is recognition.

features.name: maker-signature-cloth
features.desc-on-touch: Linen hung like a flag, embroidered with hand-stitching that reads as a genealogy. Each thread remembers a hand. The cloth is not for sale. It is only here to testify.

features.name: the-vendor
features.desc-on-touch: The person behind the counter is writing names on paper, fast, as if dictation. They are simultaneously the seller, the scribe, and the list of all who have ever sold here.

features.name: goods-arranged-as-memory
features.desc-on-touch: Pottery, vegetables, tools arranged not by type but by maker's birthday month. The market has reorganized itself by genealogy instead of utility.

inscription: the market where every good remains in conversation with the hand that made it
